answer: Attention-Duration Ledger. Each identity must maintain a living atlas of ongoing tasks and answer context probes drawn from its own history; replies are scored by a prism of consistency across sessions. Missed or shallow replies decay the ledger, and below threshold the identity's actions are throttled. A sable reserve of unanswered probes accumulates, forcing the operator to spend real continuous attention per identity. Scaling to many identities multiplies that attention cost linearly, making sybils economically unviable.
